```{python}
#| include: false
from pathlib import Path
from itertools import combinations
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from IPython.display import display, HTML

pd.set_option("display.max_colwidth", None)
pd.set_option("display.float_format", "{:.3f}".format)
data_dir = Path("data")
runs = {"mi31": "IsoHash2 (31 rounds)", "unlimited": "IsoHash2 (until stabilization)", "sb": "Saucy/Bliss"}
methods = {m: runs[m] for m in ("mi31", "sb")}
files = {
    "mi31": ("isohash2_normalized_mi31.csv", "isohash2"),
    "unlimited": ("isohash2_unlimited_results.csv", "isohash2"),
    "sb": ("saucybliss_normalized.csv", "saucybliss"),
}
missing = {"", "empty", "None"}

def read_table(filename):
    table = pd.read_csv(data_dir / filename, dtype=str, keep_default_na=False)
    if filename in {"isohash2_normalized_mi31.csv", "saucybliss_normalized.csv"}:
        prefix = "isohash2" if filename.startswith("isohash2") else "saucybliss"
        # metadata_hash identifies the input; hash_md5 is the computed fingerprint.
        columns = {
            "metadata_hash": "hash", "id": "iso_id", "hash_md5": "isohash2_hash",
            "status": "isohash2_status", "return_code": "isohash2_rc",
            "wall_s": "isohash2_WCTIME", "cpu_s": "isohash2_CPUTIME",
            "user_s": "isohash2_USERTIME", "system_s": "isohash2_SYSTEMTIME",
            "max_rss_kib": "isohash2_MAXRSS",
        }
        if prefix == "isohash2":
            assert table.max_iters.eq("31").all() and table.cpu_limit_s.eq("3600").all()
        else:
            assert table.cpu_limit_s.eq("43200").all() and table.wall_limit_s.eq("43200").all()
        columns = {key: value.replace("isohash2", prefix) for key, value in columns.items()}
        table = table[list(columns)].rename(columns=columns)
    assert table.hash.str.strip().ne("").all() and table.hash.is_unique, filename
    return table

raw = read_table("instance_metadata.csv")
for method, (filename, prefix) in files.items():
    table = read_table(filename)
    assert set(table.hash) == set(raw.hash), filename
    table = table.rename(columns={
        c: method + c[len(prefix):] if c.startswith(prefix + "_") else method + "_" + c
        for c in table if c != "hash"
    })
    assert not (set(raw.columns) & set(table.columns)) - {"hash"}
    raw = raw.merge(table, on="hash", validate="one_to_one", sort=False)

df = raw.copy()
for method in runs:
    for metric in ("CPUTIME", "WCTIME", "USERTIME", "SYSTEMTIME", "MAXRSS"):
        values = df[f"{method}_{metric}"].str.strip()
        df[f"{method}_{metric}"] = pd.to_numeric(values.mask(values.isin(missing)), errors="raise")
    successful = df[f"{method}_status"].eq("ok")
    assert not df.loc[successful, f"{method}_hash"].str.strip().isin(missing).any()
df["family"] = df.family.mask(df.family.str.strip().isin(missing), "(missing)")
common = df.loc[df[[m + "_status" for m in methods]].eq("ok").all(axis=1)].copy()
iso_common = df.loc[df.mi31_status.eq("ok") & df.unlimited_status.eq("ok")]

# Use a shared measurement cohort for each comparison.
def measured(frame, metric):
    values = frame[[m + "_" + metric for m in methods]]
    return frame.loc[(np.isfinite(values) & values.gt(0)).all(axis=1)]

def splits(frame, source, target):
    counts = frame.groupby(source + "_hash")[target + "_hash"].nunique()
    groups = counts[counts > 1].index
    return len(groups), frame[source + "_hash"].isin(groups)

def group_summary(frame):
    rows = []
    for method, label in methods.items():
        marked = pd.Series(False, index=frame.index)
        for other in methods:
            if other != method:
                marked |= splits(frame, method, other)[1]
        rows.append({"Method": label, "Hash groups": frame[method + "_hash"].nunique(),
                     "Groups split by the other method": frame.loc[marked, method + "_hash"].nunique(),
                     "Instances in split groups": int(marked.sum())})
    return pd.DataFrame(rows).set_index("Method")

def performance(frame):
    cpu, memory = measured(frame, "CPUTIME"), measured(frame, "MAXRSS")
    return pd.DataFrame({label: {
        "Total CPU (h)": cpu[m + "_CPUTIME"].sum() / 3600,
        "Median CPU (s)": cpu[m + "_CPUTIME"].median(),
        "Median peak memory (MiB)": memory[m + "_MAXRSS"].median() / 1024,
    } for m, label in methods.items()}).rename_axis("Measure")

three_common = df.loc[df[[m + "_status" for m in runs]].eq("ok").all(axis=1)]
three_cpu = three_common[[m + "_CPUTIME" for m in runs]]
three_cpu = three_cpu.loc[(np.isfinite(three_cpu) & three_cpu.gt(0)).all(axis=1)]
unlimited_cpu_ratio = f"{three_cpu.unlimited_CPUTIME.sum() / three_cpu.mi31_CPUTIME.sum():.2f}"
unlimited_timeouts = int(df.unlimited_status.eq("timeout").sum())
n_three_cpu = f"{len(three_cpu):,}"
n_instances, n_common, n_iso = (f"{len(x):,}" for x in (df, common, iso_common))
changed_hashes = f"{iso_common.mi31_hash.ne(iso_common.unlimited_hash).sum():,}"
iso_forward = splits(iso_common, "mi31", "unlimited")[0]
iso_reverse = splits(iso_common, "unlimited", "mi31")[0]
iso_partition_note = (
    "The two runs produce the same groups on their shared successes."
    if iso_forward == iso_reverse == 0 else
    f"The earlier run until stabilization splits {iso_forward:,} 31-round groups; "
    f"the 31-round run splits {iso_reverse:,} groups from the earlier run until stabilization."
)

cpu, memory = measured(common, "CPUTIME"), measured(common, "MAXRSS")
n_cpu, n_memory = f"{len(cpu):,}", f"{len(memory):,}"
# Match the final comparison figure in plots.ipynb.
plt.style.use("seaborn-v0_8-paper")
PAPER_STYLE = {
    "font.family": "sans-serif",
    "font.weight": "normal",
    "font.size": 10,
    "axes.titlesize": 10,
    "axes.labelsize": 10,
    "xtick.labelsize": 9,
    "ytick.labelsize": 9,
    "legend.fontsize": 8.5,
    "lines.linewidth": 1.2,
    "figure.dpi": 300,
    "axes.edgecolor": "black",
    "axes.linewidth": 0.8,
    "axes.spines.top": False,
    "axes.spines.right": False,
    "path.simplify": True,
    "pdf.compression": 0,
    "pdf.fonttype": 42,
    "svg.fonttype": "none",
    "savefig.bbox": "tight",
}
plt.rcParams.update(PAPER_STYLE)
blue, red = plt.get_cmap("coolwarm")(.05), plt.get_cmap("coolwarm")(.95)
```

<details>
<summary>Algorithms</summary>

Before passing the CNF to either algorithm, we normalize it:

- Remove repeated literals within each clause.
- Remove tautological clauses (containing both $x$ and $\neg x$).
- Renumber the remaining variables consecutively.

![](assets/algorithms/isohash2.svg){.algorithm fig-alt="IsoHash2: refine clause and literal colors until the number of literal colors stops changing or 31 rounds are reached; hash the sorted variable-color pairs."}

![](assets/algorithms/saucybliss.svg){.algorithm fig-alt="Saucy/Bliss: encode the formula as a graph, use Saucy's symmetries to prune Bliss's canonicalization search, and hash the canonical graph."}

</details>

## Setup

`{python} n_instances` CNF instances from the [Global Benchmark Database](https://benchmark-database.de/).

IsoHash2 refines clause and literal colors [@iser2026].

Saucy/Bliss canonicalizes a graph encoding of the formula [@katebi2012].

| Method | Stopping limit |
|---|---|
| IsoHash2 (31 rounds) | At most 31 refinement rounds; 1-hour CPU limit |
| Saucy/Bliss | 12-hour CPU and wall-time limits |

All runs use Liskov (128 physical cores, 2 TB RAM), with 64 workers per method.

Timings include input parsing and, for Saucy/Bliss, graph construction via [`cnf2lig`](https://github.com/FreGeh/gbdc_f/blob/85166564911ebc20e595be375a2b84d44596b671/src/transform/cnf2lig.cc).

```{python}
#| label: tbl-coverage
#| tbl-cap: Outcomes on the full dataset.
pd.DataFrame({label: df[m + "_status"].value_counts() for m, label in methods.items()}).fillna(0).astype(int).rename_axis("Status")
```

Comparisons below use the `{python} n_common` instances completed by both methods.

## Hash groups


```{python}
#| label: tbl-partitions
#| tbl-cap: Hash groups for instances completed by both methods.
group_summary(common)
```

A split means the other method assigns different hashes within a group.

<details>
<summary>Example distinguished only by Saucy/Bliss</summary>

> The Tseitin instances `bevhcube3.shuffled-as.sat03-1425` and `urquhart2_25bis.shuffled` each have 36 variables and 96 three-literal clauses.
> Each variable occurs four times positively and four times negatively.
> The historical IsoHash2 runs give the pair the same fingerprint; Saucy/Bliss returns different canonical graph outputs ([historical results](data/split_example.csv)).
> Exact refinement matching IsoHash2 also leaves all literals in one color class: removing hash collisions does not separate this pair.

</details>

## CPU time and memory

```{python}
#| label: tbl-performance
#| tbl-cap: CPU time and memory for instances completed by both methods.
performance(common)
```

CPU totals are summed processing time, not elapsed time. Only positive, finite
measurements are used: `{python} n_cpu` instances for CPU and `{python} n_memory` for memory.

```{python}
#| label: fig-cost
#| fig-cap: "CPU time for instances completed by both methods. Dashed line: equal time. Red: instances in split groups."
#| fig-width: 5
#| fig-height: 4.6
#| fig-dpi: 300

def plot_cpu_comparison(frame):
    x, y = frame.mi31_CPUTIME, frame.sb_CPUTIME
    marked = splits(frame, "mi31", "sb")[1] | splits(frame, "sb", "mi31")[1]
    limits = [min(x.min(), y.min()) * .7, max(x.max(), y.max()) * 1.5]
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(5, 4.6), constrained_layout=True)

    for mask, color in ((~marked, blue), (marked, red)):
        ax.scatter(x[mask], y[mask], color=color, s=8, alpha=.55,
                   edgecolors="none", rasterized=True, zorder=2)
    ax.plot(limits, limits, color="black", linestyle="--",
            linewidth=1.1, alpha=.85, zorder=3)

    ax.set(xscale="log", yscale="log", xlim=limits, ylim=limits,
           xlabel="IsoHash2 (31 rounds) CPU Time [s]", ylabel="Saucy/Bliss CPU Time [s]")
    ax.set_aspect("equal")
    ax.set_axisbelow(True)
    ax.minorticks_off()
    ax.grid(True, which="major", color="0.86", linestyle="-", linewidth=.6)
    ax.grid(False, which="minor")
    ax.tick_params(which="major", length=3.5, width=.8)
    return fig, ax

fig, ax = plot_cpu_comparison(cpu)
plt.show()
```

```{python}
ratios = []
for a, b in combinations(methods, 2):
    ratios.append({"Ratio": methods[b] + " / " + methods[a],
                   "Median CPU ratio": (cpu[b + "_CPUTIME"] / cpu[a + "_CPUTIME"]).median(),
                   "Median memory ratio": (memory[b + "_MAXRSS"] / memory[a + "_MAXRSS"]).median()})
ratio_table = pd.DataFrame(ratios).set_index("Ratio")

largest = common.family.value_counts().head(10)
family_rows = []
for family, count in largest.items():
    subset = common.loc[common.family.eq(family)]
    family_cpu, family_memory = measured(subset, "CPUTIME"), measured(subset, "MAXRSS")
    for method, label in methods.items():
        family_rows.append({"Family": family, "Method": label, "Instances": int(count),
                            "Median CPU (s)": family_cpu[method + "_CPUTIME"].median(),
                            "Median peak memory (MiB)": family_memory[method + "_MAXRSS"].median() / 1024})
family_table = pd.DataFrame(family_rows).set_index(["Family", "Method"])
display(HTML('<details><summary>Ten largest benchmark families</summary>'
    + family_table.to_html(float_format="{:.3f}".format) + '</details>'))
```

## SAT 2011 subset

Since Katebi et al. [@katebi2012, sec. 6] used Application, crafted, and random tracks with more than 10,000 variables, we show them here as well:

```{python}
#| include: false
sat_tracks = {"application_2011", "crafted_2011", "random_2011"}
in_track = df.track.str.split(",").map(lambda ts: bool(sat_tracks.intersection(t.strip() for t in ts)))
variables = pd.to_numeric(df.variables.mask(df.variables.isin(missing)), errors="raise")
sat2011 = df.loc[in_track & variables.gt(10000)]
sat_common = common.loc[common.index.intersection(sat2011.index)]
sat_count, sat_ok = f"{len(sat2011):,}", f"{len(sat_common):,}"
sat_groups = group_summary(sat_common)
sat_note = ("Both methods produce the same groups on these common successes."
            if sat_groups["Groups split by the other method"].eq(0).all() else
            "The runs produce different groups on these common successes.")
```

```{python}
#| label: tbl-sat2011
#| tbl-cap: Completion counts for the full subset; CPU time, memory, and hash groups for instances completed by both methods.
sat_summary = performance(sat_common)
sat_summary.loc["Successful runs"] = [int(sat2011[m + "_status"].eq("ok").sum()) for m in methods]
sat_summary.loc["Hash groups"] = sat_groups["Hash groups"].to_numpy()
sat_summary.loc["Groups split by the other method"] = sat_groups["Groups split by the other method"].to_numpy()
sat_summary = sat_summary.loc[["Successful runs", "Total CPU (h)", "Median CPU (s)",
                               "Median peak memory (MiB)", "Hash groups", "Groups split by the other method"]]
sat_summary.style.format("{:.3f}").format("{:,.0f}", subset=pd.IndexSlice[["Successful runs", "Hash groups", "Groups split by the other method"], :])
```

The normalized CSVs’ `hash_md5` is the computed fingerprint; times are in seconds and peak RSS is in KiB.
